kaps_punt: Plaaslike omgewingsgesondheidsprobleme: Plaaslike gesondheidsprobleme wat gereeld voorkom soos tuberkulose, diarree, malaria, masels, ensovoorts; Oorsake van gesondheidsprobleme; Simptome van gesondheidsprobleme; en Beskikbare behandeling vir gesondheidsprobleme.

items.bewering: Party siektes kom deur die lug, maar diarree kom deur vuil water, kos of hande by jou mond in.
items.blok: Hoe diarree en malaria by jou uitkom
items.bron: WHO 2014 infection-control guidelines (quoted on preventionweb.net/quick/78400): pulmonary TB is an 'obligate' and measles a 'preferential' airborne pathogen. WHO diarrhoeal disease fact sheet (who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/diarrhoeal-disease): 'Infection is spread through contaminated food or drinking-water, or from person-to-person as a result of poor hygiene.'

items.bewering: Malaria kom met 'n muskiet se byt.
items.blok: Hoe diarree en malaria by jou uitkom
items.bron: WHO malaria fact sheet (who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/malaria): 'Malaria mostly spreads to people through the bites of some infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.' Blood transfusion and needles are rare other routes, so it is right as a general statement.

items.bewering: Die omgewing maak nie hierdie siektes nie maar bring kieme en muskiete na jou. Daarom keer jy hulle by jou water en in jou huis.
items.blok: Hoe diarree en malaria by jou uitkom
items.bron: WHO diarrhoeal disease fact sheet (contaminated water, 'unsafe domestic water storage and handling is also an important risk factor'); WHO malaria fact sheet (malaria is caused by a parasite carried by mosquitoes). The mapping holds. The germ is carried by water and the parasite by the mosquito. The lesson never names the malaria parasite, but that is an omission, not a false statement.

items.bewering: Diarree begin meestal wanneer iets wat siek maak by die mond inkom. Dit is dikwels kieme uit vuil water.
items.bron: WHO diarrhoeal disease fact sheet: infection spreads through contaminated food or drinking water or through poor hygiene, which is the faecal-oral route. The quantifiers 'meestal' and 'dikwels' are supported.

items.bewering: Kieme sit ook op ongewaste hande ná die toilet.
items.bron: Western Cape Government Health (westerncape.gov.za/health-wellness/article/protect-our-children-under-5-during-paediatric-surge-season): teach children to 'clean their hands after using the toilet'; spread is person to person through poor hygiene (WHO fact sheet).

items.bewering: Hulle groei in kos wat te lank rondstaan.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food (who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639; poster reproduced at safeconsume.eu): microorganisms multiply quickly in food kept at room temperature, and cooked food should not stand for more than two hours. This is true of bacteria. Viruses do not multiply in food, but the generic plural is the same framing WHO uses.

items.bewering: 'n Vlieg dra hulle na jou kos.
items.bron: Peer-reviewed study, The Gambia (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3486903): latrine flies carried viable Shigella, Salmonella and E. coli between faeces and food, and the house fly can transmit enteric pathogens. Fly control reduced childhood diarrhoea by 23% at times when flies were numerous.

items.bewering: Die tekens en simptome is dun, waterige stoelgang wat baie kere op een dag kom. Daarby kom soms maagkrampe, opgooi en koors.
items.bron: WHO fact sheet: 'the passage of 3 or more loose or liquid stools per day'. NHS Scotland gastroenteritis guideline (clinicalguidelines.scot.nhs.uk/media/1564/gastroenteritis.pdf) and NHS Lanarkshire: diarrhoea, nausea and vomiting, crampy abdominal pain and fever are the most common symptoms. 'soms' is correct.

items.bewering: Diarree se grootste gevaar is dat die liggaam water verloor. (Ook die kop: 'Die grootste gevaar is die water wat die liggaam verloor'.)
items.blok: Die grootste gevaar is die water wat die liggaam verloor
items.bron: WHO diarrhoeal disease fact sheet, verbatim: 'The most severe threat posed by diarrhoea is dehydration.'

items.bewering: Met elke stoelgang loop water en sout uit die liggaam. Ons noem dit uitdroging as te veel water weg is.
items.blok: Die grootste gevaar is die water wat die liggaam verloor
items.bron: WHO fact sheet: 'water and electrolytes (sodium, chloride, potassium and bicarbonate) are lost through liquid stools, vomit, sweat, urine and breathing'. 'sout' is a sound simplification of electrolytes.

items.bewering: Die tekens en simptome is 'n droë mond, groot dors en min of geen urine nie. Die siek mens word moeg en slap, en 'n klein kind huil sonder trane.
items.blok: Die grootste gevaar is die water wat die liggaam verloor
items.bron: Western Cape Government Health, signs of dehydration: 'Dry or sticky mouth', 'Few or no tears when crying', 'Little or no urine', 'Tiredness', 'Thirst'. WHO fact sheet: 'drinks eagerly, thirsty' and 'lethargy'. NHS (nhs.uk/conditions/dehydration/symptoms): few or no tears, dry mouth, peeing less, tiredness.

items.bewering: Babas, klein kinders en ou mense loop die grootste gevaar om uit te droog.
items.blok: Die grootste gevaar is die water wat die liggaam verloor
items.bron: NHS (nhs.uk/conditions/dehydration): babies, children and older adults are more at risk of dehydration. HSE Ireland (www2.hse.ie/conditions/dehydration): people aged 65 and over are also at higher risk. WHO adds malnourished and immunocompromised children and people with HIV for life-threatening diarrhoea. That does not contradict the list, because the claim is about the risk of dehydration and does not say these are the only groups.

items.bewering: Roep dadelik 'n grootmens as jy of iemand anders hierdie tekens en simptome het.
items.blok: Die grootste gevaar is die water wat die liggaam verloor
items.bron: Western Cape Government Health: if a child shows any symptoms of dehydration, 'seek help at your nearest clinic' and 'Do not wait in line'. A child who follows this exactly calls an adult at once, which is safe and in line with the guidance.

items.bewering: Gaan kliniek toe, veral gou met 'n baba of klein kind.
items.blok: Wat om te doen as iemand diarree het
items.bron: City of Cape Town (capetown.gov.za, 'Diarrhoea cases spike amid surge season'): seek help at the clinic and do not wait for danger signs. Western Cape Government Health says the same. Taken literally it is a safe instruction. NHS Scotland notes that most children can be cared for at home, so going to the clinic is cautious rather than strictly required, but it is not wrong.

items.bewering: Baie mense glo dat iemand met diarree minder moet drink. Hy moet juis meer as gewoonlik drink.
items.blok: Wat om te doen as iemand diarree het
items.bron: Belief: Kenya, Nyando study (BMC Public Health, doi 10.1186/s12889-015-2127-1): more than 70% of mothers gave less fluid during diarrhoea. HIFA: the belief that fluids should be stopped is common in Africa, Latin America and South Asia. Instruction: WHO IMCI Plan A, 'Give extra fluid for diarrhoea and continue feeding' (PAHO IMCI job aid, paho.org/sites/default/files/IM-JobAids-2005-06eng.pdf). The belief is not shown with a South African figure, but 'baie mense' is a general claim and it is well supported.

items.bewering: Die kliniek se spesiale drankie sit water en sout terug.
items.blok: Wat om te doen as iemand diarree het
items.bron: WHO fact sheet: ORS is 'a solution of clean water, sugar and salt'. Western Cape Government Health: 'free oral rehydration solutions (ORS) available at our clinics'.

items.bewering: 'n Grootmens kan vooraf by die kliniek of 'n gesondheidswerker vra hoe om so 'n drankie aan te meng as die kliniek ver is.
items.blok: Wat om te doen as iemand diarree het
items.bron: SA Road-to-Health booklet promotes a home sugar-salt solution (SAJCH, scielo.org.za/pdf/sajch/v7n3/02.pdf). Western Cape Government Health gives the recipe: 1 L boiled, cooled water, half a level teaspoon of salt, 8 level teaspoons of sugar. The instruction is safe. Mixing is left to an adult who has asked a health worker, so a child does not mix by guesswork, and a wrong salt amount is a real risk.

items.bewering: Die drankie is die belangrikste deel van die behandeling en word voor en ná die kliniekbesoek gedrink tot die diarree ophou.
items.blok: Wat om te doen as iemand diarree het
items.bron: WHO fact sheet: dehydration is the most severe threat and 'Diarrhoea should be treated with oral rehydration solution (ORS)'. Zinc is an addition that shortens episodes by 25%, so it does not displace ORS as the most important part. WHO rehydration plan reproduced by MSF (medicalguidelines.msf.org/en/node/663): give liquid 'until diarrhoea stops'. Western Cape Government Health: take ORS 'along on the way to the clinic'.

items.bewering: Die siek mens hou ook aan eet, en 'n baba hou aan borsdrink.
items.blok: Wat om te doen as iemand diarree het
items.bron: WHO fact sheet: continue 'nutrient-rich foods – including breast milk – during an episode'. MSF/WHO plan: 'Breastfeeding should always be continued.' Western Cape Government Health: 'Do not stop offering food or milk feeds.'

items.bewering: 'n Baba, klein kind en iemand wat uitgedroog lyk of alles opgooi, moet beslis kliniek toe.
items.blok: Wat om te doen as iemand diarree het
items.bron: Western Cape Government Health danger signs include 'Not drinking, or vomiting everything', and any dehydration sign means going to the clinic. The instruction is safe if followed literally.

items.bewering: Was jou hande met seep ná die toilet en voor jy kos hanteer of eet.
items.bron: WHO fact sheet lists 'hand washing with soap' as a key prevention measure. Western Cape Government Health: clean hands after the toilet and before and after meals.

items.bewering: Handewas met seep is een van die goedkoopste maniere wat werk.
items.bron: Cairncross & Valdmanis, 'Water Supply, Sanitation, and Hygiene Promotion', Disease Control Priorities 2nd ed. (World Bank, 2006), cited via globalhandwashing.org and LSHTM: hygiene promotion including handwashing costs US$3.35 per DALY averted, the cheapest of the diarrhoea interventions compared (latrine promotion $11.15, ORT $132-2,570). Reviews put the effect at a 30-47% reduction in diarrhoea. The softened 'een van die' is correct. The figure is a modelled estimate from 2006, so do not strengthen it to 'die goedkoopste'.

items.bewering: Hou drinkwater toe en skink dit uit sonder om hande of 'n beker in die water te steek.
items.bron: CDC safe water storage guidance (stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/79547): a covered container with a small opening, and pouring rather than dipping in with a possibly contaminated object. WHO fact sheet: unsafe domestic water storage and handling is an important risk factor.

items.bewering: Maak kos vars klaar en hou dit toe.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food (keep food at safe temperatures; do not leave cooked food standing). Western Cape Government Health: warm weather spoils food quickly. Covering food keeps flies off it (see the fly item above).

items.bewering: Hou die toilet skoon en weg van waar julle water skep.
items.bron: IFRC epidemic control toolkit (epidemics.ifrc.org/pdf/176): at least 30 m between latrines and water sources. A UNHCR document notes that the distance varies with ground conditions, and the SA groundwater protocol recommends at least 75 m (DFID DEWPoint review of national regulations). Western Cape Government Health: keep toilets clean.

items.bewering: Malaria kom van 'n sekere muskiet wat meestal snags byt.
items.bron: WHO malaria fact sheet: 'some infected female Anopheles mosquitoes' ('n sekere muskiet is correct). Public Health Agency Northern Ireland malaria factsheet (publichealth.hscni.net) and Infonet-Biovision: Anopheles bite mostly between dusk and dawn, with peaks that vary by species, so 'meestal' is right. 'kom van' is read with the next sentence, which makes clear the mosquito carries the disease rather than originating it.

items.bewering: Die muskiet dra dit van 'n siek mens na 'n gesonde een.
items.bron: CDC malaria biology: the mosquito is infected by feeding on an infected person, and the parasite develops in it for 10-21 days before it can infect someone else. WHO: malaria 'does not spread from person to person'. The lesson does not say it does, and the carrier picture is accurate.

items.bewering: Muskiete broei in water wat stilstaan.
items.bron: CDC mosquito life cycle (cdc.gov/mosquitoes/pdfs/anopheleslifecycle-eng.pdf): eggs are laid in water and the first three stages are aquatic. African Entomology 24 (2016) 421-431, eastern Mpumalanga: An. arabiensis breed in rain puddles, hoof prints and residual pools left as rivers recede, all still water.

items.bewering: Malaria kom meestal in die warm en nat maande voor.
items.bron: National Department of Health (health.gov.za/outbreaks-malaria): cases rise in October, peak in January and February and wane towards May. NICD (via Cape Times 2023): the rainy summer season increases the number of malaria-carrying Anopheles.

items.bewering: Dit kom hoofsaaklik in die laer, warm dele in die noordooste van Suid-Afrika voor.
items.bron: National Department of Health: Limpopo, Mpumalanga and KwaZulu-Natal are endemic, 'mainly transmitted along the border areas'. NICD scientist J. Raman (Cape Times, 31 Oct 2023): risk is in the 'low altitude shared international border regions' of those three provinces, the lowveld and northern KZN. Those are the low, warm north-eastern parts.

items.bewering: Die meeste mense woon nie daar nie maar kan dit kry as hulle daar gaan kuier.
items.bron: National Department of Health: '10% of the population (approximately 4.9 million persons) is at risk'. UP Institute for Sustainable Malaria Control: just over 10% live in endemic areas. NICD urges travellers to risk areas to be tested for flu-like illness afterwards (sanews.gov.za/node/66237).

items.bewering: Malaria voel soos griep met koors, koue rillings en groot moegheid. Dit kan saggies begin. Hoofpyn en lyfpyne kom daarby, en party mense gooi op.
items.blok: Hoe malaria voel en wat jy doen
items.bron: CDC malaria symptoms (cdc.gov/malaria/about/symptoms_malaria.html): 'Fever and flu-like illness', 'Chills', 'Headache, muscle aches, and tiredness', 'Nausea, vomiting'. WHO: first symptoms 'may be mild ... and difficult to recognize as malaria'. Mapping: the flu comparison is the one NICD itself uses ('people often describe as flu-like'). The one way it could mislead is a learner deciding it is only flu and staying home. The same block blocks that at once with 'Gaan gou kliniek toe' and 'Vertel ... dat jy in 'n malariagebied was', so the mapping holds.

items.bewering: Die tekens en simptome begin eers 'n week of langer ná die byt.
items.blok: Hoe malaria voel en wat jy doen
items.bron: CDC: 'The incubation period in most cases of malaria ranges from 7 – 30 days', and some species stay dormant for months. WHO: usually 10-15 days. NICD: test anyone ill after a risk area in the past 10 days to three weeks, and up to six months after travel. 'n week of langer' matches the CDC floor and every longer window.

items.bewering: Gaan gou kliniek toe as jy hulle kry. Vertel by die kliniek dat jy in 'n malariagebied was.
items.blok: Hoe malaria voel en wat jy doen
items.bron: NICD via SAnews (sanews.gov.za/node/55901; node/68554): people with fever or flu-like illness after a risk area should be tested urgently, and patients should always tell their healthcare provider about recent travel. Safe if followed literally.

items.bewering: Die kliniek toets met 'n prikkie bloed, en malaria kan genees word.
items.blok: Hoe malaria voel en wat jy doen
items.bron: NICD via SAnews: testing is by blood smear microscopy or rapid diagnostic test. South Africa has used finger-prick HRPII rapid tests since 2001 (Malaria Journal 2007, Limpopo, doi 10.1186/1475-2875-6-74). WHO and the National Department of Health: 'preventable and curable'.

items.bewering: Dit kan vinnig ernstig word as 'n mens wag.
items.blok: Hoe malaria voel en wat jy doen
items.bron: WHO malaria fact sheet: untreated P. falciparum 'can progress to severe illness and death within 24 hours'. In South Africa most infections are P. falciparum (Malaria Journal 2007).

items.bewering: Slaap in 'n malariagebied onder 'n muskietnet.
items.bron: Public Health Agency Northern Ireland malaria factsheet and Bankmed/UP ISMC bite-prevention guidance (search results for 'Malaria 101 bite prevention', up.ac.za): bed nets, screens and repellent are the bite-prevention measures. Safe if followed literally.

items.bewering: 'n Grootmens smeer afweermiddel aan jou arms en bene, weg van jou hande, oë en mond.
items.bron: CDC mosquito bite prevention (cdc.gov/mosquitoes/prevention): adults apply repellent to children; 'Do not apply repellent to a child's hands, eyes, mouth, cuts, or irritated skin.' A child who follows this exactly has an adult do it and keeps it off hands, eyes and mouth, which matches CDC.

items.bewering: Hou vensters en deure saans toe of sit gaas voor.
items.bron: CDC mosquito bite prevention: 'Use screens on windows and doors' and repair holes so mosquitoes stay outside. Closing windows and doors at the evening biting time is the same barrier.

items.bewering: Trek teen sononder lang moue en 'n lang broek aan.
items.bron: CDC: 'Wear loose-fitting, long-sleeved shirts and pants'. Public Health Agency Northern Ireland malaria factsheet: cover up from dusk because Anopheles bite between dusk and dawn.

items.bewering: diarree: Dun, waterige stoelgang wat baie kere op een dag kom.
items.bron: WHO: 'the passage of 3 or more loose or liquid stools per day'. Read alone the entry is accurate. 'baie kere' is a fair rendering of three or more.

items.bewering: uitdroging: Wanneer die liggaam te veel van sy water verloor het.
items.bron: NHS (nhs.uk/conditions/dehydration): dehydration is when the body loses more fluid than it takes in. Read alone the entry is accurate.

items.bewering: kieme: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster kids' entry (via merriam-webster.com/medical/germ search result): 'a microscopic living thing, especially one that causes disease'. Vocabulary.com: 'a minute life form'. Dictionary.com: 'a microorganism, especially when disease-producing'. Caveat for a person, not a fault: whether viruses (rotavirus is a major cause of child diarrhoea) count as living is genuinely debated among biologists (ASU Ask A Biologist; Warwick 'edge of life'). The entry follows the standard dictionary sense and 'kan' avoids claiming what every germ does.

items.bewering: simptoom: Iets wat wys dat 'n mens se gesondheid skeefloop en wat hy self ervaar, soos pyn, moegheid of naarheid.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters, 'Understanding disease signs and symptoms', and Wikipedia 'Signs and symptoms': symptoms are subjective experiences reported by the person. Pain, tiredness and nausea are standard examples. Read alone the entry is accurate.

items.bewering: teken: Iets wat wys dat 'n mens se gesondheid skeefloop en wat 'n ander mens self kan sien, hoor, ruik of meet, ook al vertel hy niks, soos 'n uitslag of koors.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters lists fever and rash as signs, objective indicators that others can observe. Fever counts as a sign when it is measured (a thermometer reading), which is the sense here ('meet'). Read alone the entry is accurate.

items.bewering: malaria: 'n Siekte wat 'n mens van 'n sekere muskiet se byt kry.
items.bron: WHO malaria fact sheet: spread 'through the bites of some infected female Anopheles mosquitoes'. Read alone the entry is accurate. It does not name the parasite, which is an omission, not an error.

items.bewering: muskietnet: 'n Fyn net wat oor 'n bed hang en muskiete weghou.
items.bron: CDC mosquito bite prevention (netting keeps mosquitoes out) and the Public Health Agency Northern Ireland factsheet (bed nets). Read alone the entry is accurate.

items.bewering: afweermiddel: Goed wat op die vel gesmeer word sodat muskiete nie byt nie.
items.bron: CDC mosquito bite prevention: repellent is applied to exposed skin to prevent bites. Repellent can also be sprayed on clothing, but 'gesmeer op die vel' describes the main use and 'sodat' states the purpose. Read alone the entry is accurate.

items.bewering: kliniek: 'n Plek in die gemeenskap waar mense gesondheidsorg kry, of hulle siek is of gesond.
items.bron: Western Cape Government Health: clinics give free ORS and treat sick children, and also give catch-up immunisations and vitamin A from the Road to Health booklet, which is care for the healthy. Read alone the entry is accurate.

items.bewering: Parallelle stel: die diarree-blokke (oorsaak, tekens, gevaar, behandeling, voorkoming) en die malaria-blokke (oorsaak, tekens, behandeling, voorkoming), saam gelees.
items.blok: Hoe diarree en malaria by jou uitkom / Waar malaria vandaan kom / Hoe malaria voel en wat jy doen / Hoe jy diarree keer / Hoe jy muskietbyte keer
items.bron: Tested as a set against the sources above, and no false contrast was found. Both send the sick person to the clinic quickly, consistent with Western Cape Health and NICD. Both use 'tekens en simptome' in a way consistent with the two glossary entries. The routes are kept apart correctly: diarrhoea through the mouth, malaria through a bite, and neither is said to spread through the air. The prevention lists match their own routes: hands, water, food and toilet for diarrhoea, and net, repellent, screens and clothing for malaria. The one asymmetry is that diarrhoea is said to come from 'kieme' while the malaria blocks never say a tiny living thing causes malaria. That leaves the cause of malaria at 'a mosquito carries it', which is incomplete but not false.

opsomming: Elke nagaanbare bewering, al vyf oortreffende trappe, die griep-vergelyking en al nege begrip-inskrywings (elkeen alleen gelees) is teen WHO, CDC, die NICD, die Nasionale Departement van Gesondheid en die Wes-Kaapse Gesondheidsdepartement bevestig, en elke voorkomings- en behandelingsopdrag is veilig as 'n kind dit letterlik volg; vir 'n mens om te weet, nie 'n fout nie: 'kieme' word as lewende dinge omskryf terwyl virusse se status as lewend omstrede is, en die les noem nie die malaria-parasiet nie.
